title: Keypeer
description: A password manager that lives entirely in the browser. No server, no account, no network calls: the vault is encrypted on your machine and the key never touches disk.
highlights: AES-256-GCM per entry, key derived with Argon2id and held only in background-worker memory
Login-form detection for one-click autofill and save prompts
Idle auto-lock, encrypted export/import, Vitest unit tests for crypto and storage
terminal: idle timeout ─► key wiped ─► vault locked

title: JobOps
description: Contributor to a self-hosted job-search platform with 800+ users that reached #3 on GitHub Trending for TypeScript.
highlights: Built the WUZZUF and Khamsat job-board extractors with unit-tested parsers
Wired both into the Docker build and the extractor health checks

title: Git-Pulse
description: Turns any GitHub profile into an RPG character sheet: level, class, rank tier, achievements and a repo-hygiene radar, plus an AI-written roast.
highlights: Scoring logic written as pure, unit-tested functions over the GitHub REST API
LLM roast via Groq with a deterministic fallback when no key is set
Client-side PNG card export on canvas

title: Gahez
description: Interview practice that adapts to the role you pick. Five questions, one at a time, with scored and specific feedback after each answer.
highlights: Each answer scored on relevance, clarity, structure, specificity and confidence
Works with no account; bring-your-own Anthropic, OpenAI or Gemini key
Static site, no backend, responsive down to phone
imageAlt: Gahez feedback screen scoring an interview answer

title: TrackWatch
description: An ESP32 smartwatch prototype that reads heart rate, body temperature and motion and shows them live on an OLED screen.
highlights: MAX30102, MPU-6050 and DS18B20 over I2C and OneWire at ~100 ms polling
8-hour stress runs with no crashes or sensor dropouts

title: Hospital Management System
description: Desktop hospital app covering registration, scheduling, medical records and billing. I led the 7-person team from Figma designs to a working Qt6 GUI.
highlights: Appointment booking with automatic double-booking checks
Billing with per-clinic pricing and insurance discounts
Object-oriented C++ with Qt6, sub-200 ms UI response on CRUD operations
